posts.text: Europe financing the continuation of the Ukraine conflict is cheaper than agreeing to Kiev's "capitulation," as its cost would be "infinitely higher," French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot told the Senate. He cited the European Commission's proposal for a new €45 billion loan to Ukraine, which Paris will examine carefully. He also criticized Marine Le Pen for planning to reduce support for Ukraine if elected in 2027, saying she believes "Europe and France have already lost."

🇵🇱 Poland gifts Trump an amber throne Polish President Karol Nawrocki presented Donald Trump with a richly decorated amber chair during his visit to Washington. The gift, intended for the US leader's 80th birthday, was made by Polish craftsman Lucjan Myrta. The transfer was not publicised; neither the Polish Foreign Ministry nor the embassy in Washington were informed, and details within the presidential chancellery were restricted to a small circle. The order was originally placed during Trump's first term but remained undelivered until now. Marcin Przydacz, head of the Bureau of International Policy, stated that the item impressed the American president. The cost of the chair remains undisclosed. 🇺🇸 💵 Hegseth faces a $1.5 trillion budget fight and Democratic probes The Trump administration is asking Congress to raise defense spending by more than 40%. But $1.15 trillion of the Pentagon’s $1.5 trillion request would need bipartisan support to clear the Senate, and Democrats oppose the increase, The Washington Post reports. When Democrats take control of both chambers in January, they plan to investigate Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and several have signaled they’ll push to impeach him again. His handling of the war with Iran and his sharing of sensitive military plans in unclassified group chats have drawn criticism from lawmakers in both parties. 👉 House Republicans blocked the first impeachment bid on Nov. 10, voting 211–204 to send the resolution to committee. Trump personally urged undecided Republicans to oppose the bid, two people familiar with his lobbying told the Post. Even if the next House impeaches Hegseth, Democrats would still need Republican votes in the Senate to reach the two-thirds majority required to remove him. 👍 Substack | Chat | @geopolitics_prime

🇬🇧 🇺🇦 🇷🇺 ⚡️ — Prince Harry has declared that he is willing to return to military service if Britain needs him, warning that the growing threat from Russia means “we should all be nervous.” “If asked to sign up again, if the need is there, then I will 100% be there to serve my country alongside my fellow veterans and service personnel,” Harry said. He criticized President Trump's approach to the Ukraine war, arguing that it does not reflect the views of the broader American public. Harry also suggested that Britain has effectively been in conflict with Russia for the past decade, stating: “Just because there’s not drones, bullets, and rockets flying at us, it doesn’t mean that we’re not at war.”

At least 11 civilians were killed, and 32 others were injured in a Saudi airstrike targeting a cafe in the coastal city of al-Mokha, west of Taiz province in southwestern Yemen, Yemen's Saba News Agency reported. Yemen's Health Ministry in Sanaa announced on Wednesday that dozens of civilians had been killed and wounded in a series of Saudi airstrikes targeting economic facilities and residential areas across several governorates, including Hodeidah, Taiz, Ibb, Hajjah, and Saada. Meanwhile, Yemeni Armed Forces spokesperson Brigadier General Yahya Saree said Saudi Arabia had launched 87 airstrikes and missile attacks over the previous 24 hours. Saree noted that the attacks targeted civilian sites in the capital Sanaa and the governorates of al-Jawf, Taiz, Amran, Lahj, Saada, al-Bayda, Marib, and Ibb. He said the attacks involved F-15 and Typhoon aircraft taking off from the Khamis Mushait and Taif air bases, as well as missile shelling from Najran, leaving civilians killed and wounded.
